title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Cooperating with the Public Security Organs in Carrying Out the Campaign to Eliminate the "Six Evils"
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Cooperating with the Public Security Organs in the Campaign to Eliminate the "Six Evils"

Fa (Ban) Fa [1989] No. 34

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

The Central Committee has decided to launch a nationwide unified campaign from late October to around the Spring Festival of next year to eliminate the "six evils": prostitution and whoring, producing, trafficking, and disseminating obscene articles, abducting and trafficking women and children, privately cultivating, consuming, and trafficking narcotic drugs, gathering for gambling, and using feudal superstition to cheat people of property. On November 13, 1989, the State Council held a telephone conference to make arrangements for this unified campaign. People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the arrangements of this telephone conference, fully play their role as judicial organs, actively participate in and cooperate with this unified campaign.

In recent years, under the leadership of Party committees, people's courts at all levels have lawfully tried a large number of criminal cases involving the "six evils" and severely punished the offenders. However, the momentum of the spread and development of such crimes has not yet been effectively curbed. For example, from January to August this year, courts nationwide accepted a total of 1,294 cases of manufacturing, trafficking, and smuggling of narcotic drugs, an increase of 18.11% over the same period last year; they accepted 325 cases of producing, trafficking, and disseminating obscene articles, an increase of 34.3% over the same period last year. The spread of these six types of social ills and criminal activities has seriously corrupted social morals, interfered with reform and opening up and the construction of spiritual civilization, harmed the physical and mental health of the general public, especially young people, and has become a destabilizing factor affecting public security. They are six major "public hazards" deeply detested by the people and must be resolutely and effectively addressed. To ensure the success of this campaign, the following requirements are specifically put forward:

1. Strengthen leadership and carefully organize. For this unified campaign, all localities shall establish specialized leadership teams headed by the public security organs, with the participation of responsible persons from the procuratorial and court departments. Courts at all levels shall, under the unified deployment of the specialized teams, closely cooperate with all relevant departments, actively participate in the special campaign to eliminate the "six evils", and treat the trial of criminal cases involving the "six evils" as an important task in criminal adjudication work for this winter and next spring, to be carried out with diligence. The principal leading comrades of courts at all levels shall personally take charge of this work, pay attention to overall planning, careful organization, and shall strengthen and allocate trial personnel to ensure the smooth progress of this unified campaign.

2. Concentrate forces and strike at key targets. The nine key targets for this unified campaign are: (1) those who entice (including procuring), shelter, or force women into prostitution; (2) those who engage in prostitution or whoring and refuse to reform despite repeated education; (3) those who smuggle, produce, traffic, or organize the dissemination of obscene articles in relatively large quantities; (4) those who use obscene articles to instigate or entice others to commit crimes or disseminate obscene articles to minors under the age of 18; (5) those who abduct and traffic women and children by fraudulent and violent means; (6) gambling ringleaders who gather others for gambling, those who make a living by gambling, and habitual gamblers who refuse to reform despite repeated education; (7) those who use feudal superstitious means to rape women or cause death; (8) the ringleaders and key members of reactionary secret societies; (9) those who smuggle, traffic, or transport narcotic drugs, those who privately cultivate large quantities of opium poppy or illegally process drugs, and those who consume drugs and refuse to reform despite repeated education. Courts at all localities shall, under the unified deployment of the special leadership teams for eliminating the "six evils", clarify the key targets for attack and determine the trial policy based on the actual circumstances of their respective regions.

3. Promptly try criminal cases involving the "six evils" without delay. For cases already submitted to the court, people's courts at all localities shall, under the premise of ensuring case quality, improve trial efficiency as much as possible. For major and significant cases with great impact, courts may intervene in advance to understand the facts. Once the case is filed with the court, trial shall be conducted promptly. As long as the basic facts are clear and the basic evidence is conclusive, and a conviction can be established, a judgment shall be rendered in a timely manner according to law, without entangling in minor issues that do not affect the determination of guilt or the measurement of punishment.

4. Fully utilize legal weapons to severely crack down on criminals. When trying such cases, courts at all localities shall maintain a resolute attitude while also paying attention to policy, strictly distinguishing the line between crime and non-crime. In recent years, the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate have issued a series of judicial interpretations, resolving prominent issues in the application of law for conviction and sentencing, including in crimes involving the "six evils". When trying criminal cases involving the "six evils", courts at all localities shall carefully study and implement these judicial interpretations, accurately apply the law, and effectively punish offenders of the "six evils". At the same time, attention shall be paid to studying new situations and new problems encountered in trials. Questions concerning how to apply the law for conviction and sentencing shall be reported promptly with opinions, level by level, to the Supreme People's Court, so that further judicial interpretations can be issued to better meet the needs of the campaign to eliminate the "six evils".

5. Closely coordinate with the unified campaign and conduct public hearings and public sentencing at opportune moments. Courts at all localities shall, at different stages of this unified campaign, hold as many sentencing conferences as possible in areas where "six evils" cases are frequent, in order to deter and disintegrate criminals, inspire and educate the people, expand the momentum of the unified campaign, and curb the continued spread of the "six evils".

6. Monitor the trends of the campaign and manage information work. This unified campaign covers a wide scope and involves complex circumstances. Courts at all localities shall closely monitor developments and promptly report to higher courts on the situation of trying "six evils" cases, problems encountered in the application of law, and the analysis and handling of typical cases. Information work must be of high quality and speed, and must not miss opportunities.

7. Combine trial work with active participation in comprehensive governance to eliminate the "six evils". While trying criminal cases involving the "six evils" according to law, people's courts at all localities shall, based on problems exposed in the cases, promptly submit judicial suggestions to the relevant units, urging the localities and units where the crimes occurred to strengthen management, plug loopholes, eliminate blind spots, and prevent and reduce the occurrence of "six evils" crimes and social ills.

November 13, 1989
